context: The binary tree has seven nodes. Root 1 has left child 7 and right child 3. The left-hand 7 has children 4 and 5. Node 3 has left child 6 and right child 7. Nodes 4, 5, 6, and the rightmost 7 are leaves.
The task is to find and record every node with value 7, so the search continues after the first match. The two 7s highlighted in teal lie on different branches and represent distinct node objects.
description: A dashed green arrow traces the depth-first traversal around the binary tree. The orange dot to the left of each node marks the preorder visit: check the node’s value upon entry, then recursively visit its left and right subtrees in that order.

The full preorder sequence is [1, 7, 4, 5, 3, 6, 7]. Whenever a node has value 7, append it to the results and continue exploring. After finding the left-hand 7, the search still visits its children 4 and 5.

frames.explanation: The code stores two node objects in res: first the root’s left child 7, then the right child 7 of node 3. Their values are [7, 7], representing distinct positions in the tree.
frames.title: Check for and record matches on preorder visits

summary: Visit all seven nodes in root–left–right order. Record the root’s left child 7 first, then the right child 7 of node 3.
title: Finding and recording every node with value 7 in preorder
